assays.assay_description: Mice received a single dose of DOI (1 mg/kg i.p.) 24 h after LPS or saline pretreatment and were observed for 15–20 minutes; the number of head-twitches was counted as a measure of 5-HT2A receptor function.

application_type.evidence: Mice received a single dose of DOI (1mg/kg i.p.)

setup_habituation.evidence: No apparatus habituation specific to the HTR test is described

time_to_assay.evidence: Mice received a single dose of DOI (1mg/kg i.p.) and were observed for 20 minutes

outcomes.summary: DOI induced head-twitch behaviour in both saline- and LPS-pretreated mice. LPS administered 24 h before DOI significantly enhanced the head-twitch response compared with saline pretreatment, consistent with increased 5-HT2A receptor function.
outcomes.evidence: DOI had a significant effect on head-twitch behaviours in animals treated with both saline and LPS, however, this was elevated in animals receiving a single dose of LPS 24 hours before, compared to those receiving DOI alone (p < 0.05; Fig 4B).

judge_notes: Only the DOI head-twitch assay involves psychedelic administration to rodents; LPS-only behavioural assays (OFT, EPM, FST, sucrose preference, marble burying, locomotor) were excluded as no psychedelic compound was administered for those tests.
All three candidates agreed on a single HTR assay; consolidated using modal values.
B1 set to 0 (1 measure = 0 points per rubric; glm candidate's score of 1 was incorrect).
Session duration in methods states 20 min (Fig 4B caption says 15 min); used 20 min per Methods, both fall in 15–60 min bin → score 1.
